clue.text: Concerned with a particular science, working in lab coat

indicators.note: working here means the letters are worked over, set going in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scientist is busy at the bench wearing a lab coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges IN plus LABCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany is the study of plants, so the adjective describes anything relating to that one science.

clue.text: A chimney at home has a particular chemical

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney
in means at home, as in 'staying in tonight'

explanation.surface: A household chimney turns out to contain some specific chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is a Scots word for a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumina is aluminium oxide, one specific compound used in refining metal and making abrasives.

clue.text: Managed head of cattle the man had bred on farm

parts.note: ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the word cattle

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
'd is the short form of had, as in he'd

explanation.surface: A man managed a herd of cattle that he had raised on his farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' gives just D, the contraction in 'he'd'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ranch animals is to raise them on a large farm, so the past tense means bred on a farm.

clue.text: What sounds like short time of prayer

indicators.note: what sounds like says the entry is spoken the same as a word meaning short

parts.note: terse means short or curt in speech

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about something resembling a brief period of prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Terce is one of the canonical hours of the Christian divine office, said at the third hour of daylight.

clue.text: Troubled clodhopper gets given food outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for being given food goes round the clumsy oaf

parts.note: fed means given food
a lummox is a clumsy, awkward person, like a clodhopper

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf is upset even though someone has fed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flummoxed means being baffled or thrown into confusion, a state of being mentally troubled.

clue.text: Hear the deer — not all gone to ground

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Listen to the deer, though some of them have bolted into cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox that has earthed has taken refuge in its burrow, which is what going to ground means in hunting.

clue.text: Famous paper editor presenting a short news item

indicators.note: short means the word for a news item loses its final letter

parts.note: a story is a news item in a paper

explanation.surface: A celebrated newspaper editor puts forward a brief news report.
explanation.walkthrough: David Astor was the long-serving editor of The Observer, a British Sunday paper.
explanation.definitionFit: David Astor edited The Observer for nearly three decades and is the best-known journalist of that wealthy family.

clue.text: Traditional worker at one time hit hard

parts.note: smit is an archaic past form of smite, meaning struck, so it is hit as said long ago
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned labourer who once struck something forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: SMIT is an old form of 'smote'; 'at one time' flags the archaism.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith forging metal at an anvil is the classic old craft trade, hence a traditional worker.

clue.text: Vet possibly taking dog with hesitation

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A veterinary surgeon hesitantly takes on a dog as a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A vet heals sick animals, so is one example of a healer; 'possibly' signals the example.

clue.text: City with abbey entertaining Rome's foremost theologian

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest inside, so the city wraps round the letter

parts.note: Bath is an English city famous for its abbey and Roman baths

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of the word Rome's

explanation.surface: An abbey city plays host to Rome's leading religious thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a Somerset city with a famous abbey. The theologian was a Swiss Protestant, not a Roman Catholic, which the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Barth was a twentieth-century Swiss Protestant thinker, among the most influential writers on Christian doctrine.

clue.text: Be quiet, hugging tart after reversing vehicle

indicators.note: after reversing says the assembled letters are read from the end back to the start
hugging means holding inside, so the first pair of words wrap round the word for tart

parts.note: acid means tart or sour
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: An order to keep silent while embracing a sour person, then backing out in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' puts ACID inside BEP to give BACIDEP, which 'after reversing' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered rickshaw carrying passengers, so it is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: What's drunk agreed on, imbibing a soft drink

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so the shuffled letters swallow the single letter
drunk means the words agreed on are scrambled, as if in a state of intoxication

explanation.surface: A question about which beverage people settled on, with the drink being non-alcoholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges AGREEDON, and 'imbibing' takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fizzy citrus beverage containing no alcohol, the kind called a soft drink.

clue.text: Wader, last of those being watchable to all in this lake

indicators.note: being here means one letter becomes another, the final letter turning into the film rating

parts.note: a heron is a long-legged wading bird

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word those

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A wading bird, open to view by everyone, stands at this lake.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for films fit for all ages; it replaces the E, the last letter of 'those'.
explanation.definitionFit: Huron is one of the five Great Lakes on the border of the United States and Canada.

clue.text: Scandinavian king knocked over by busy person gets cross

parts.note: a bee is proverbially busy, so a busy person is a busy bee

indicators.note: knocked over means toppled, so the king's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Olaf is the name of several kings of Norway

explanation.surface: A Norse monarch is toppled by a hard worker who becomes angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is a noun, a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a hybrid bred from domestic cattle and the American bison, so it is a cross between breeds.

clue.text: Lie about Conservative leading to row

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a line is a row, as of people or seats

explanation.surface: A falsehood about a Tory politician sparks a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but is a line; 'Lie' is to rest, not a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back or lie down at rest, the verb sense of lie.

clue.text: Entertained, hosting meal for politicians in the London area

indicators.note: hosting means having guests inside, so the word for entertained goes round the other pieces

parts.note: had, as in had people round, means entertained
MPs are Members of Parliament
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone threw a party with a dinner for MPs in part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' as in 'had friends over' gives entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampstead is a leafy district in north London known for its heath.

clue.text: Act as official leader for the deprived

parts.note: to be something is to act in that role
ref is short for referee, a match official

indicators.note: leader for picks the first letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Someone serves as a guiding official on behalf of the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means having lost something precious, so a dispossessed person is deprived.

clue.text: Dine out and get sloshed, lacking the ability to speak properly

definitions.text: lacking the ability to speak properly

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, so the words dine out and get are mixed up

explanation.surface: A night out with dinner and drinking leaves someone slurring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloshed' rearranges DINEOUT plus GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tongue-tied means being unable to get words out, through shyness or confusion.

clue.text: One among special men, he, a husband and a man of God

indicators.note: special here means the letters are given an unusual arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a stays as written and H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A list: a single man among a select group, a husband, and a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges MEN and HE to NEHEM; 'among' sets I, the Roman one, with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nehemiah is an Old Testament figure who rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem, a devout leader of the Jews.

clue.text: Not genuine without ancient script

parts.note: cod means mock or fake, as in a cod accent
ex is a Latin word meaning out of or without

explanation.surface: A fake document lacking its supposedly old writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A codex is an early manuscript volume, so it holds old handwritten text.

clue.text: The French female working for top lady as cleaner

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of the
under means serving beneath someone
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A French woman works for the lady of the house as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who washes and irons clothes and linen is one kind of cleaner.

clue.text: Mouth's opening and nothing more, say, for this?

definitions.text: Mouth's opening and nothing more, say, for this?

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word Mouth's

parts.note: to utter something is to say it

explanation.surface: A question about speech made with the lips barely parted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes speaking with the mouth scarcely open; 'and nothing more' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To mumble words under the breath, barely opening the lips, is exactly the low indistinct speech described.

clue.text: Support clown putting out rubbish

indicators.note: putting out means ejecting, so the word for rubbish is removed

parts.note: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Backing a clown who is taking the bins out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar or column that holds up a bridge or arch, a structural support.

clue.text: Initially cold, a person making advances becomes smoother

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word cold

parts.note: a lender advances money as loans

explanation.surface: A suitor is coldly received at first, then becomes more suave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' suggests romance; here it is loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A calender is a machine of rollers that presses cloth or paper flat and glossy.

clue.text: Something behind the teeth like a pip friend swallowed

parts.note: a fruit pip is tough and unyielding, so something like one is hard
a pal is a friend
ate means swallowed food

explanation.surface: A diner bites on something stuck behind the teeth, like a pip a friend gulped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' looks like a containment signal but simply gives ATE at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony front part of the roof of the mouth lies just behind the upper teeth.

clue.text: Ultimately, you loathe B&B's frightful salad

indicators.note: frightful suggests a dreadful mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder
ultimately picks the final letter of the word you

parts.note: the two letters B and B from the bed-and-breakfast abbreviation, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A guest at a bed and breakfast is offered a salad they find awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges U (from 'Ultimately, you') with LOATHE and BB.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabbouleh is a Levantine dish of bulgur wheat, parsley, mint and tomato, served cold as a side.

clue.text: In one part of the country there's a very soft sort of stone

indicators.note: In says the following pieces are placed inside the word for a region

parts.note: a shire is a county, a part of England
a means one, as in a single item
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft

explanation.surface: In a certain county there is an unusually soft kind of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is pianissimo in music; 'very soft' sounds like a description of the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a precious gem, a blue variety of corundum, so a kind of stone in the jeweller's sense.

clue.text: A hundred affectionate types who work for charities?

definitions.note: read as people who work for charities, a noun phrase

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
huggers are people who show affection by embracing

explanation.surface: A crowd of warm-hearted people are perhaps charity volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuggers are street fundraisers who stop passers-by for direct-debit pledges; the word blends charity and muggers. The question mark marks the jokey sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid street fundraisers signing up donors are slangily called by this name, a blend of charity and mugger.

clue.text: Cooked having first got tin open

indicators.note: having first got puts the word for a tin at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: a can is a tin
did, as in did the vegetables, means cooked

explanation.surface: Someone cooked after first opening a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' is the adjective frank, not the verb a tin-opener performs.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and honest, being open about one's views.

clue.text: Spy catches second person up further on

indicators.note: catches means holds inside, so the spy's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional spy

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ye is the old second-person plural pronoun

explanation.surface: A spy apprehends someone who has gone ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the old pronoun because this is a down clue, read from bottom to top; Bond is the classic fictional spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond means farther away, at a point past something else.

clue.text: Printing unit knocked off end of white book

indicators.note: knocked off end of says the printing unit is removed from the tail of the word for white

parts.note: albumen is the white of an egg
an en is a printer's unit of measure, half an em

explanation.surface: A printing machine has been knocked off the end of a white book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' is egg white, ALBUMEN; EN, half an em, is a typesetting measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a blank book for keeping photographs, stamps or autographs.

clue.text: Joint with fracture — avoid cold initially

indicators.note: avoid means the letter is left out of the word for fracture

parts.note: a crack is a fracture

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word cold

explanation.surface: A broken joint, with advice to keep away from cold at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is a cut of meat, as in a rack of lamb, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack of lamb or pork is a cut of meat, a joint for roasting.
